newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN CHIEF MEETS DENKTASH TO BRIDGE CYPRUS GAP.
newsitem.headline: UN CHIEF MEETS DENKTASH TO BRIDGE CYPRUS GAP.

text.p: U.N. chief Kofi Annan met Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash on Wednesday as part of his initiative to resume direct talks between Greek and Turkish Cypriots.

Amid growing tensions on the divided island and fears of a military build-up, international pressure has been building up for a solution to the decades-old Cyprus problem ahead of the possible start of talks on its joining the European Union.

Denktash, head of the breakaway northern Turkish Cypriot state recognised only by Ankara, said he hoped direct talks could resume by June at a venue to be proposed by Annan -- "either Geneva or New York or somewhere else.

"We are in Annan's hands. We are for negotiations," he said after meeting Annan at the U.N.'s European headquarters in Geneva. The London-trained lawyer cautioned against the involvement of too many outside mediators: "Too many cooks spoil the broth."
U.N. resident representative in Cyprus Gustave Feissel warned that the gap between the two communities would be even harder to bridge if Cyprus started EU membership talks in 1998.
He told reporters that Annan wanted the Security Council and the EU to support the latest U.N. initiative.

"Time is running out. The EU issue makes it all the more urgent," Feissel said. "If these (EU) negotiations begin before a settlement, the world may be a very different one from the one now. That's bad news for everybody.
"If we can't bring these people on board beforehand, it will be very difficult to do that afterwards."

The United Nations has had a peacekeeping force in Cyprus, divided since Turkey invaded the northern third in 1974 after a coup sponsored by Athens, since 1963. A small army of mediators has failed for decades to reunite Cyprus under a federal umbrella.
